Modern.tagline: Hats made on the block, in the city.
Modern.brandNameRationale: The crown is the part of a hat that sits on the head — the structural centre of every hat ever made. Strongest of Agent A's modern row: Brim Studio is fine but the brim is secondary, Felt & Form is too abstract. Crown & Co. is a clean two-word wordmark that names the most important part of the object and reads like a credible modern hatter without referencing the protected legacy houses (Lock, Stetson, Borsalino).
Modern.industrySummary: Modern hat-making in 2025+ sits between the heritage houses (Lock & Co, Stetson, Borsalino) and the streetwear caps (New Era). The opening is for a small-batch modern hatter that makes a tight range — a fedora, a panama, a flat cap — and posts the hatter's name. Customers are 30-50, dress better than their friends, and want a hat made for their head.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Lock & Co. (lockhatters.com) holds the heritage tier at 350 years. Stetson (stetson.com) holds the western-American legacy. Optimo Hats (optimo.com) is the closest modern peer in Chicago. We sit smaller, urban, and made-to-order.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern hatter making a tight range, to the head.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Dresses with intent. Owns a good overcoat. Has wanted a real fedora since their twenties and is finally going to do it. Will travel for the fitting.
behaviors: Books a fitting and a measure
Asks about felt weight and rabbit-vs-beaver
Wears the hat the day they get it

dos: Name the hatter who blocked the hat

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — CROWN & CO. set in a precise modern serif. A small abstract crown form (the top of a hat seen from above) sits as the favicon and the inside-band stamp. The mark is foil-stamped into the leather sweatband.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: Söhne for the booking and body
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the hatter-craft register; Söhne keeps the booking modern.

Luxury.tagline: Felt hats in the Alessandria tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Alessandria, Piedmont is the home of Italian hat-making — Borsalino was founded there in 1857, and the town's hat industry predates and outlasts any single house. Strongest of Agent A's place row for luxury: St James's Block borrows from Lock & Co's actual address, Cuenca Panama is correct for panamas only. Alessandria is the city that defines Italian felt and is itself unbranded, sidestepping the Borsalino TM that Agent A flagged.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury hat-making serves the customer who already owns the Borsalino and the Lock and wants the next one bespoke. The opening is a small Italian-tradition hatter making to measure, with a register that nods to Piedmont craft rather than mass production.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Borsalino (borsalino.com) holds the Italian heritage. Lock & Co. (lockhatters.com) is the English peer at 350 years. Worth & Worth (hatshop.com) is the New York bespoke peer. We sit smaller and Alessandria-rooted.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Bespoke felt hats in the Alessandria tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 70. Owns a Borsalino and a Lock. Travels with a hat box. Will pay for the bespoke, the felt sample, and the fitting in person.
behaviors: Books a fitting six months ahead
Keeps the hat in a wooden box

dos: Refer to felt by mill and grade
Send a paper hatband-card with each delivery

Minimal.tagline: A hatter. One block at a time.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: The brim is the second structural part of a hat — and 'brim' is one syllable. Strongest minimal mark of Agent A's modern row: Crown & Co. is two words (used for the modern slot), Felt & Form is too abstract. Brim alone — single English word, names the object, reads on a sign in any city.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal hat-making is a workshop, a block, and a hatter. The opening is a maker who publishes the range, the price, and the wait time, and ships when the hat is done. Customers want a real hat, not a brand.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Optimo Hats (optimo.com) holds the minimal-bespoke peer. Worth & Worth (hatshop.com) competes in NYC bespoke. Local independent milliners compete on relationship. We publish less than any of them.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A hatter. Three shapes. Published prices.

targetAudience.primary: Adults 30-55 who want a single hat — fedora, panama, or flat cap — made to fit. They don't want the brand. They want the hat to last twenty years.
behaviors: Reads the price list before booking
Sends the hat back for a re-block in year ten

dos: Publish the three shapes and the prices
Confirm the order in one sentence

Corporate.tagline: A multi-shop hat-making partnership in the Coke tradition.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: William Coke commissioned the original bowler (the 'Coke hat') in 1849 from Lock & Co — making the Coke surname the anchor of the bowler's history without using the Lock & Co name. Strongest of Agent A's heritage row for corporate: Beaver & Felt is craft but not corporate, Bowler & Crown reads single-shop. Coke Brothers carries the surname seriously and lands as a partnership-style group, well clear of any active TM.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate hat-making in 2025+ is small as a category — most consolidation is in hat-and-cap distribution rather than craft. The opening is for a partnership-model group that brings together independent hatters under a serious wholesale-and-bespoke umbrella, positioned on craft seniority.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Bollman Hat Co. (bollmanhats.com) holds the US heritage manufacturing tier. Stetson (stetson.com) is the legacy western peer. New Era (neweracap.com) holds the licensed-cap distribution. We sit smaller, partnership-model, and craft-led.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A clinician-led — sorry, hatter-led — partnership in the Coke tradition.

targetAudience.primary: Buyers at luxury department stores, costume directors at major productions, and independent hatters considering joining a group. They sign multi-season contracts and care about craft quality, delivery, and master-hatter retention.
behaviors: Reviews craft sample boards before signing
Values master-hatter retention as a signal

dos: Lead with master-hatter retention and craft KPIs
Speak the language of wholesale buyers and costume

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark — a single bowler-hat silhouette in cross-section — to the left. Reads cleanly on uniforms, signage, and wholesale decks.

typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed quarterly letters
typography.rationale: Inter scales cleanly across wholesale decks; the serif handles the printed letters.

Creative.tagline: A hatter's workshop. The block makes the hat.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The milliner's block is the wooden form, hand-carved per size, that gives a hat its crown shape — the foundational tool of the trade. Strongest of Agent A's craft row for creative: Sweatband & Crown is two parts but not the tool, Toquilla Weave is panama-only. The Milliner's Block names the actual tool that every hat is made on, and reads as a designed workshop in the register of a printer's-shop or a luthier's bench.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative hat-making sits in the register of a designed printer's shop or a small luthier — the workshop is the brand. Customers are design-literate, often in adjacent crafts, and want a hat made on a real block by a hatter they can name. The opening is a brand with print-shop, illustrated, tool-rich identity.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Optimo Hats (optimo.com) holds the design-led peer in Chicago. Worth & Worth (hatshop.com) competes in NYC bespoke. Larose Paris (laroseparis.com) is the closest editorial-design peer. We sit warmer, more workshop-honest.
Creative.positioningStatement: A hatter's workshop organised around the block.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a chunky display serif with letterpress impression. The O of BLOCK is set as a small woodblock-style hat-block in cross-section. A standalone block mark for stickers and the hatbox tag.
